text:
Edmonton had the game won before the first intermission ended. EDM scored four times in the opening 20 minutes, including a 14:26 snap shot from Owen Michaels and Evan Bouchard's goal sixteen seconds later, and out-chanced VAN 1.53 to 0.14 in expected goals. Bouchard's came on a chance under 1%. Leon Draisaitl made it 5-0 at 0:27 of the second, and Connor McDavid and Kasperi Kapanen added shorthanded goals to reach 8-2. McDavid finished with a goal and four assists.

The rally was real, though it came from a team trailing by six. VAN outscored EDM in the final two periods, and its third-period expected goals (1.84 to 0.53) show a team pressing a lead that was already gone. Marco Rossi scored twice, at 1:53 and 4:43, and Elias Pettersson's power-play slap shot at 7:37 made it 8-6. Draisaitl answered on the power play at 9:26, and Jamie Oleksiak's goal at 18:31 cut it to 9-7. Rossi finished with two goals and an assist in 15:18.

The goalies decided the shape of it. Kevin Lankinen allowed eight goals on 21 shots, 5.73 more than the chances deserved, and Devon Levi gave up seven on 22 shots, 4.09 worse than expected. EDM's 57% claim to deserve the win is modest for a nine-goal night, and VAN had the better even-strength expected goals, 2.45 to 1.89. That tells you the scoreboard ran well ahead of the play, and the first period decided it. The teams meet again after VAN's 6-5 overtime win on September 29.
